answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprinting. Each identity commits a hash of its recent action graph, and continuity requires the new epoch’s graph to overlap the prior one above a threshold. A sybil cluster must therefore operate every fake identity through a spiral of consistent, costly interactions across epochs, not a one-time registration. Mismatches trigger quarantine and forfeiture of accumulated copper rewards. The trellis of historical links makes each maintained fake identity cost real compute and transaction fees indefinitely.
